summaries.summary:
Title: Water Pipeline Project Complaints

Residents of Ward 9 and Ward 3 are voicing complaints regarding a recent water pipeline project conducted by Sagar Infra. Complaints from Ward 9 include low water pressure on Lake Road, especially in the mornings, and a three-day water supply interruption while the new pipeline was being connected. Additionally, residents reported a scooter accident on Lake Road caused by a trench left by the project, and a lack of warning signs after the road was dug up. Complaints from Ward 3 highlighted the presence of potholes on Canal Street after the project, despite an improvement in water pressure on Canal Street due to the new pipeline. Title: Nehru School Plot Issue & Citizen Portal Downtime

Residents of Ward 5 are complaining about stagnant water on an empty plot behind Nehru School, which they claim causes mosquito bites for the children attending the school. Nehru School has requested the corporation to fill the plot and spray for mosquitoes before the monsoon peaks. Simultaneously, Ward 1 shopkeepers are requesting the corporation to waive late fines due to the downtime of the citizen portal, which affected trade licence renewals. Citizens in Ward 1 also reported missing tracking numbers on complaints filed during the portal outage, raising concerns about the transparency and efficiency of the corporation's response to the problem.

Title: Temple Street Illumination Issue

In Ward 11, there is a persistent problem with the streetlights on Temple Street being dark for a month, despite the presence of a bus stop on the same street. Brightway Electricals, the maintenance contractor employed by the Ward Corporation, claims it is waiting for new LED fittings to fix the issue, which has led to a reported chain-snatching incident on the dark street. Additionally, Ward 12 has a similar problem with the streetlights on the Temple Street extension, where the timer has not been fixed by Brightway Electricals. Citizens are expressing safety concerns due to the darkness on Temple Street, especially after dark.

Title: Blocked Drain Complaints in Ward 4

Residents of Ward 4 are complaining about a blocked drain on Station Road, which has caused standing water to accumulate near the bus depot. This has led to a mosquito infestation and a reported doubling of fever cases in the area, with the Station Road health centre attributing the health issue to the blocked drain. Residents are requesting the fogging team to control the mosquito problem.

Title: Ward 2 Garbage Collection and Trade Licensing Issues

In Ward 2, there are ongoing issues related to waste collection and trade licensing. Citizens are complaining about the failure to collect garbage for four days after new segregation rules started, and mixed waste being refused by collection staff despite households not being informed about the new rules. Additionally, traders at Gandhi Market are complaining that the smell from overflowing bins is deterring customers, and a fine was issued to traders for late trade licence renewal due to a downed citizen portal. All these issues seem to be interconnected, affecting the cleanliness and trade operations in Ward 2.

Title: Stray Dogs and Irregular Garbage Pickups Affecting Ward 7

Residents of Ward 7 are complaining about stray dogs tearing open garbage bags left on Mill Road due to irregular garbage pickups. Additionally, a child was bitten by a stray dog on Mill Road near the garbage heap, and residents are requesting a door-to-door awareness drive on Circular 14/2026 segregation rules to address the issue.

Title: Mixed Waste Collection Issue in Ward 7

Residents on Mill Road in Ward 7 are facing issues related to mixed waste collection, as highlighted by a series of complaints tied to the enforcement of Circular 14/2026. Collection staff are refusing mixed waste, which has led to confusion among households who claim they were not informed about the new segregation rules. This has caused residents to seek a door-to-door awareness campaign to better understand the regulations. Additionally, the irregular collection schedules have attracted stray dogs to Mill Road, resulting in incidents such as a child being bitten by a stray dog near the garbage heap. Efforts to communicate the changes effectively to the affected households and to improve the collection schedules

Title: Birth Certificate Delay in Ward 8

Residents of Ward 8 are complaining about a delay in receiving their birth certificates, which has taken 20 days. Additionally, there is confusion due to the counter stating that the printer is broken, which may be affecting the issuance process. This issue involves the citizens of Ward 8 and the city corporation responsible for handling birth certificates.

questions.q: What were the main problems residents complained about across the city in July 2026?
questions.rag:
Residents across the city in July 2026 had several complaints:

- In Ward 7, there was a request for a door-to-door awareness drive concerning the segregation rules on Circular 14/2026.
- Ward 4 had a health centre on Station Road reporting a doubling of fever cases this month, with residents attributing the problem to a blocked drain.
- Ward 11 encountered a series of issues on Temple Street, including a chain-snatching incident after dark, six streetlights being dark for a month, and women feeling unsafe walking home from the bus stop due to the darkness.

These issues reflect a combination of social awareness, health concerns, safety on the streets, and maintenance problems within the city's different wards.
